Hi all, I'm trying to understand the issue here when i define instance as follows lean server 

instance {α β : Type} [Add β ]:
  Add  (α → β) where
  add (f g) x := (f x )+ (g x)


example : (fun x ↦ x + 1) + (fun x ↦ x * 2) = (fun x ↦  x + 1 + (x * 2)) := by
  funext x
  rfl

The above works with no issues but when i change the instance to 

instance {α β : Type} [Add β ] (f :α → β ) (g :α → β ):
  Add  (α → β) where
  add (f g) x := (f x )+ (g x)

this doesn't work in lean server as the error is related to instance arguments. But this instance works in my local but the example doesn't compile. I'm not able to understand how is instance working. Also what exactly is the role of [Add β] : Add (α → β), I tried googling and asked LLM to answer this but they were not convincing (or i couldn't understand). Can anyone help me out on this and how exactly this works?

The first instance is mathematically super clear, it says that if you have two types α and β with an addition on β, then the type α → β also has an addition (defined in the obvious way).

The second one says that, if you have two types α and β with an addition on β and two functions f g : α → β, then the type α → β also has an addition: this definition is the same as before, and in particular it does not depend on f and g (the fact that you use the same name is irrelevant, f and g in the third line are unrelated to f and g in the first line). Is this really what you want? I don't think so.

The error message says the following: Lean is complaining that to apply the second instance, every time it will need to find an addition on α → β it will have to guess two functions f g : α → β (even if they are not used in the definition of addition they appear in the type of the declaration, so Lean has to guess them), and it says "I have to way of guessing them, so this is a bad instance".
This topic was moved here from #general > understandig instance behaviour by Riccardo Brasca.

How does it even work in your local? Are you sure your local version is up-to-date?

My understanding is that instance is used to let Lean automatically fill in a desired proof/structure (which will be the proof/construction in the instances in your imports) of the form [myClass myObject] without even explicitly asking Lean to do so. So it is not mathematically wrong to have explicit arguments in instance, it just says explicit arguments should not be used in instance because it does not make sense for automation.

I don't understand your question. It doesn't work in the online editor, that uses the last version of lean.

Concerning instance, yes, it used to let Lean automatically find the thing for you. What Lean is telling in the second case is "I will never find this, since I have no way of guessing what f and g are". Note that, as I said, f and g are not the function you are adding.
